concepts.name: Logarithms and iterated logarithm notation
concepts.gloss: The base-2 logarithm lg n = ceil(log2 n), its rules (log of a product, change of base), and the meaning of powers such as (lg n)^(1-kappa).

concepts.name: Big-Omega, Theta and little-o notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic lower bounds Omega, tight bounds Theta and strictly smaller order o, used alongside O to compare running times.

concepts.name: Binary representation and bit operations
concepts.gloss: Writing non-negative integers (and signed ones in two's complement) as bit strings, and the bitwise operations XOR, AND and shifts, including the number of ones in a bit string.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers modulo m, congruence classes, and the cyclic group Z/m under addition.

concepts.name: Primes, coprimality and gcd
concepts.gloss: Prime numbers, greatest common divisors, pairwise coprime integers, and the fact that primes of a given size are plentiful and can be found by search.

concepts.name: Chinese remainder theorem
concepts.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli, the map from Z/(m1...mk) to the product of Z/mi given by reduction is a bijection (ring isomorphism).

concepts.name: Roots of unity
concepts.gloss: The complex solutions of z^n = 1, namely e^{2πik/n}, with Euler's formula e^{iθ} = cos θ + i sin θ and the fact that their powers sum to zero in the nontrivial case.

concepts.name: Vectors, matrices and invertibility
concepts.gloss: Vectors, linear maps and matrices over R, C or F2, matrix products and inverses, triangular and permutation matrices, and linear combinations.

concepts.name: Finite field F2 arithmetic
concepts.gloss: The field with elements 0 and 1 in which addition is XOR and multiplication is AND, over which vector spaces of bit vectors are studied.

concepts.name: Permutations and Cartesian products
concepts.gloss: Bijections of finite sets, product index sets [a1]x...x[at], and listing multi-indexed arrays in lexicographic (row-major) order.

concepts.name: Floor, ceiling and summation notation
concepts.gloss: Rounding down and up, finite and geometric sums, and indicator notation.

concepts.name: Recurrences and induction
concepts.gloss: Defining a cost by a recurrence, bounding it by induction or unrolling, and the divide-and-conquer pattern T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n).

concepts.name: Norms, absolute values and error bounds
concepts.gloss: The modulus of a complex number, the maximum norm of a vector, the triangle inequality, and how to bound accumulated rounding errors and then round to the nearest integer.

concepts.name: Fast Fourier transform and divide and conquer
concepts.gloss: The standard O(n log n) evaluation of a length-2^k DFT by splitting into halves, and its use to multiply polynomials via pointwise products.

concepts.name: Sorting and data movement on tapes
concepts.gloss: Ordinary sorting and merging of lists, and the idea that a tape machine reads and writes sequentially, so rearranging data costs scans rather than random access.

concepts.name: Finite alphabet encodings and constant-factor simulation
concepts.gloss: Storing data in a fixed finite alphabet, packing a constant number of symbols per cell, and simulating one machine by another with a constant-factor time change.

concepts.name: Ring and group notions for polynomials
concepts.gloss: Sets with addition and multiplication satisfying the usual laws, polynomial reduction modulo a fixed polynomial, and maps preserving both operations.

subset-intersection-labels.name: label
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: A label, the smaller member of a nested pair $U\subset V$.

subset-intersection-labels.quote: $X_a$ has source $U_a$ and sink $\mathcal F,$ $Y_a$ has source $0$ and sink $U_a^\perp,$ and scratch roles have source $0$ and sink $\mathcal F.$

subset-intersection-labels.name: input count
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The number of inputs $a$, each contributing one source dimension.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: Each $U_a$ is a line, so sources total $N,$ one per input, and sinks $Wm-N.$

subset-intersection-labels.name: stage index
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The index of the current stage, which exposes the $j$th tensor factor.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: At stage $j$ let $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},$ $R=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle$ and $B=R^\perp$ in $A.$

subset-intersection-labels.name: stage space
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The tensor space $F^{\otimes(j-1)}$ at stage $j$.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: At stage $j$ let $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},$ $R=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle$ and $B=R^\perp$ in $A.$

subset-intersection-labels.name: stage line
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The line spanned by the first $j-1$ triple tensors.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: At stage $j$ let $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},$ $R=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle$ and $B=R^\perp$ in $A.$

subset-intersection-labels.name: stage complement
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The complement $R^\perp$ of $R$ inside $A$.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: At stage $j$ let $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},$ $R=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle$ and $B=R^\perp$ in $A.$

subset-intersection-labels.name: invocation count
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The number of invocations of the repeated block.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: With $\nu$ invocations of $c$ central wires each, total loss $L=\nu ch.$

subset-intersection-labels.name: central wires
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The number of central wires in one invocation.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: With $\nu$ invocations of $c$ central wires each, total loss $L=\nu ch.$

subset-intersection-labels.name: total loss
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The total dimension lost on decreasing edges.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: With $\nu$ invocations of $c$ central wires each, total loss $L=\nu ch.$

subset-intersection-labels.name: orthogonal sum
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The orthogonal direct sum of two subspaces.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: Gate labels at times $0$ to $7$ are $B\otimes\langle t_T\rangle,$ $B\otimes F,$ $(B\otimes F)\oplus(R\otimes\langle t_T\rangle),$ $A\otimes F,$ $B\otimes F,$ $(B\otimes F)\oplus(R\otimes\langle t_T\rangle^\perp),$ $A\otimes F,$ $A\otimes F,$ with $\oplus$ the orthogonal sum.

subset-intersection-labels.name: total edge rank
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The total rank of all edge changes.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: Bit network: $-P_{U_a}$ replaces $M_v$ at the source of $X_a;$ then $P_{U_a^\perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m$ makes every endpoint difference $I_m.$ Edge ranks equal dimension changes, except at the $N$ source edges, where $2P_{U_a}$ has rank one. Write $s$ for the total edge rank, so $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}m.$

subset-intersection-labels.name: two-point kernel
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The matrix $H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H$.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: Complex network: $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=\alpha I+\beta\sigma,$ with $H$ the Hadamard matrix, $\alpha=\frac{1+i}{2},$ $\beta=\frac{1-i}{2}$ and $\sigma$ the coordinate swap.

subset-intersection-labels.name: Hadamard matrix
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The normalized Hadamard matrix.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: Complex network: $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=\alpha I+\beta\sigma,$ with $H$ the Hadamard matrix, $\alpha=\frac{1+i}{2},$ $\beta=\frac{1-i}{2}$ and $\sigma$ the coordinate swap.

subset-intersection-labels.name: kernel coefficient
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The coefficient $\frac{1+i}{2}$ of the identity in $C$.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: Complex network: $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=\alpha I+\beta\sigma,$ with $H$ the Hadamard matrix, $\alpha=\frac{1+i}{2},$ $\beta=\frac{1-i}{2}$ and $\sigma$ the coordinate swap.

subset-intersection-labels.name: kernel coefficient
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The coefficient $\frac{1-i}{2}$ of $\sigma$ in $C$.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: Complex network: $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=\alpha I+\beta\sigma,$ with $H$ the Hadamard matrix, $\alpha=\frac{1+i}{2},$ $\beta=\frac{1-i}{2}$ and $\sigma$ the coordinate swap.

subset-intersection-labels.name: coordinate swap
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The matrix that interchanges the two coordinates.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: Complex network: $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=\alpha I+\beta\sigma,$ with $H$ the Hadamard matrix, $\alpha=\frac{1+i}{2},$ $\beta=\frac{1-i}{2}$ and $\sigma$ the coordinate swap.

subset-intersection-labels.name: phase frame
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The phase frame of label $U$ on functions of binary vectors.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: Frames over binary $x$ are $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m},$ with $q_U(x)=|P_Ux|\bmod4$ and $|\cdot|$ the Hamming weight.

subset-intersection-labels.name: phase exponent
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The phase exponent $|P_Ux|\bmod 4$ of label $U$.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: Frames over binary $x$ are $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m},$ with $q_U(x)=|P_Ux|\bmod4$ and $|\cdot|$ the Hamming weight.

subset-intersection-labels.name: binary vector
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: A binary vector in $\mathbb F_2^m$.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: Frames over binary $x$ are $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m},$ with $q_U(x)=|P_Ux|\bmod4$ and $|\cdot|$ the Hamming weight.

subset-intersection-labels.name: Hamming weight
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The number of ones in a binary vector.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: Frames over binary $x$ are $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m},$ with $q_U(x)=|P_Ux|\bmod4$ and $|\cdot|$ the Hamming weight.

subset-intersection-labels.name: orthonormal basis
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: An orthonormal basis of the residual $E$.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: For an orthonormal basis $\mathcal K$ of a residual $E,$ $q_V(x)-q_U(x)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal K}|w|\,(w\cdot x\bmod2)\pmod4,$ with $|w|$ odd.

subset-intersection-labels.name: residual
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The orthogonal residual of an edge.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: For an orthonormal basis $\mathcal K$ of a residual $E,$ $q_V(x)-q_U(x)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal K}|w|\,(w\cdot x\bmod2)\pmod4,$ with $|w|$ odd.

subset-intersection-labels.name: basis vector
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: A vector of the orthonormal basis $\mathcal K$.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: For an orthonormal basis $\mathcal K$ of a residual $E,$ $q_V(x)-q_U(x)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal K}|w|\,(w\cdot x\bmod2)\pmod4,$ with $|w|$ odd.

subset-intersection-labels.name: translation
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The translation by a binary vector $w$.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: Each factor $i^{\pm(w\cdot x\bmod2)}$ is a kernel $\alpha I+\beta\tau_w$ or its inverse, since $H\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)H=\sigma$ turns $(-1)^{w\cdot x}$ into a translation $\tau_w.$

subset-intersection-labels.name: sign matrix
subset-intersection-labels.meaning: The diagonal sign matrix $\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$.
subset-intersection-labels.quote: The pair $X_a\to Y_a$ has inverse kernels, which $C=iZC^{-1}Z$ with $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ turns into $C,$ so every role carries $C^{\otimes m}.$
The labels are attached to the gates and terminals of a [Linear exchange network with restored scratch wires](linear-network.md).
They are used as frames in [Frames on wire arrays](common-frame-principle.md): vertex $v$ carries $M_v=P_{U_v}.$
The labels are based on [Rank, subspaces and orthogonal complements](linear-algebra-basics.md).

background.summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes and coprimality, the Chinese remainder theorem, permutations, induction, recurrences), calculus-level analysis (logarithms, floor and ceiling, norms and rounding errors), linear algebra (vectors, matrices, invertibility, rank, over the reals, complex numbers and F2), and algorithms (asymptotic notation, schoolbook multiplication, divide and conquer, sorting) with a first look at the FFT. They know basic multitape Turing machines and tapes, polynomials and complex numbers including roots of unity. They have not met Schoenhage-Strassen or Karatsuba-level multiplication algorithms in depth, ring and group-algebra language beyond polynomials, tensor products, numerical error analysis of fixed-point transforms, or any research literature on integer multiplication.
